FRET measurements are very powerful tools for studying biomolecules, but that their analysis requires a careful assessment of the assumptions underlying the data analysis and that the analysis of FRET data can be greatly improved by the combination of analytical and simulation methods.
FRET is a powerful tool to study protein dynamics and structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accuracy of FRET-based distance measurements is limited by dye mobility and fluorescence quenching, and that these effects can be accurately accounted for in the analysis of FRET data.

the combination of molecular simulations, graphical analysis, and analytical modeling is a very powerful tool to extract accurate and precise DA distances from FRET measurements of labeled macromolecules and to resolve the underlying structural dynamics.

the quasiquantitative FRET-induced donor fluorescence intensity decays, εD(t) = D(t) − Dref(t)/Aref(t), can be used for a fast and accurate analysis of FRET experiments in the homogeneous quasistatic case, and we provide a general analysis framework for more complex heterogeneous cases, where dye states can be related to protein structures by simulations.
